---
title: "Fair Learning — Labs"
---

Six hands-on notebooks in two parallel tracks, mirroring the
[dependence labs](../../dependence/labs/index.qmd).  The verb is **remove**: every
lab is the objective $\text{loss} = \text{fit} + \mu\,\operatorname{Dep}(\hat y, S)$
with a different $\operatorname{Dep}$ or a different real-world $S$.

## Learn-the-Tool Track

Build each removal method in isolation, on controlled synthetic data where you
know the right answer, before touching real applications.

| Lab | Topic |
|-----|-------|
| [Tool 1 — Drop & orthogonalize](lab-tool1-drop.qmd) | why dropping $S$ leaks; linear neutrality and its hole |
| [Tool 2 — The CKA penalty](lab-tool2-cka-penalty.qmd) | close the hole; sweep $\mu$; read the frontier |
| [Tool 2.5 — The Gaussianize-first trap](lab-tool2.5-gaussianize-first.qmd) | why only *conditional* Gaussianization buys fairness |
| [Tool 3 — Adversarial removal](lab-tool3-adversarial.qmd) | the learned $\operatorname{Dep}$ and its instability |

## Do-the-Job Track

Task-shaped deliverables on real data.

| Lab | Deliverable |
|-----|-------------|
| [Job A — Validate your tools](lab-jobA-validate.qmd) | calibration sheet: each method against a known answer |
| [Job B — Neutralize an income model](lab-jobB-neutralize-credit.qmd) | fairness on real US Census income data |
| [Job C — Beta-neutralize a strategy](lab-jobC-beta-neutral.qmd) | factor-neutrality on the real S&P basket |

## Shared Setup

Every lab starts with the same imports:

```python
import sys, pathlib
sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path.cwd() / "src"))
from lectures import plotting, datasets
from lectures.measures import cka_rbf, cka_linear
from lectures.neutralize import fair_fit       # closed-form teaching stand-in
plotting.set_style("notes")

# the end-to-end version (Tool 2 §3 and Job B) — the course's real library
import os
os.environ["KERAS_BACKEND"] = "jax"            # set BEFORE importing keras
import keras
from fairkl import FairModelWrapper            # loss = fit + μ·CKA(ŷ, S)
```

The do-the-job labs additionally load real data with
`datasets.load_credit()` (Job B) and `datasets.load_returns()` (Job C).
